subject: Preflight: regional capacity acceptance & autoscale prechecks for SageWave Dedicated
messages:
From: Olga Petrov <olga@redwood.com>
To: Alex Rivers <alex@sagewave.ai>, Jules Martin <jules@cloudops.sagewave.ai>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 20 Oct 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Preflight: regional capacity acceptance & autoscale prechecks for SageWave Dedicated

Hi Alex / Jules —

Short version: before we kick provisioning for the Dedicated GPU pool, we need your sign-off on the region pair, burst policy guardrails, and the network/IP allowlist. Attaching a short preflight checklist and our recommended autoscale/burst defaults based on your expected QPS and max concurrent sessions.

Key asks for this week:
- Confirm preferred primary/secondary regions (we recommend us-west-2 primary + us-east-1 failover for latency & cost balance).
- Confirm maximum burst headroom required (we propose 30% burst from reserved pool for the first 90 days).
- Share the CIDR(s) for the VPC peering and the IP ranges for your load balancer so we can provision the NV peerings and firewall rules.
- Approve the attached preflight checklist so we can schedule the pool turnup (target window: Nov 3-5).

Notes on technical defaults we've chosen for the proposal:
- GPU flavor: NVIDIA A100s (80GB) for transformer work; we can switch to H100 on request but that will change cost profile.
- Autoscale policy: 2x baseline buffer, 1.5x burst multiplier, 10s scale-up window, 5m scale-down cool-down. This keeps warm KV cache copies for 99th percentile latency while controlling cold-start tail.
- Cache policy: prefix KV caching for session reuse; we'll enable per-customer cache partitioning to reduce cross-tenant eviction.

I've included Monica and Karthik to coordinate timelines and the network runbook. If you confirm region + burst headroom, we can lock the provisioning ticket and send the SOW addendum to Procurement.

Thanks,
Olga
Olga Petrov
Implementation Lead, Redwood Inference

Thanks Olga — this is great and granular, appreciate it. Quick answers from our side: 

- Region: agree with your recommendation (us-west-2 primary, us-east-1 secondary). Our latency-sensitive traffic is mostly west-coast and EU is low volume for now.
- Burst: 30% headroom is fine for Q1; we may need to revisit if we onboard feature flags that increase concurrency.
- Network: attaching our current network diagram and the LB egress ranges. Jules, can you confirm the CIDR you'd like Redwood to peer with?

Procurement, please note this will be an SOW addendum to the existing Dedicated agreement (DEAL-8527). Once Olga confirms the turnup window, we can schedule the kickoff.

Couple of small questions for the team: 
1) Can Redwood provide an estimated per-hour cost delta if we switch to H100 in the first 30 days? (need for internal approval).
2) How will KV cache warm-up work on day-of-turnup? Is there a recommended warm-up script or bench we should run?

I'll wait for Karthik/Olga to confirm and will loop Procurement once we have dates.

—Alex

Thanks team — quick technical notes and the warm-up plan below. Apologies for the long email but wanted to capture everything to avoid back-and-forth during the activation window.

Summary of decisions and actions (we'll track these in the Drive folder linked above):
- Regions locked: us-west-2 (primary), us-east-1 (failover).
- Burst headroom: 30% for 90 days; we’ll run weekly usage reviews and adjust if needed.
- GPU flavor: A100 (80 GB) for turnup. H100 cost delta estimate attached; escalate if you prefer H100.

Network & security prechecks (pre-turnup):
- Provide target VPC CIDR for peering: please confirm the CIDR by EOD Mon, Oct 25.
- Open the following egress ports on your firewall for our peering subnets: 9000-9100 (control plane), 443 (TLS), 10250 (k8s node API).
- Confirm whether mTLS is required between the customer LB and Redwood edge; if yes, we'll exchange certs during the week before turnup.

Autoscale & burst specifics:
- Baseline target nodes: sized for your average token/sec from the telemetry you shared (config attached).
- Scale-up policy: trigger at 75% CPU or 70% gRPC pending requests sustained for 10s. Add burst nodes up to 30% of reserved pool.
- Scale-down: remove burst nodes after 5 minutes of sustained low utilization; KV eviction policy runs every minute with LRU bias to keep session-affine keys.

Warm-up runbook (short):
1) Pre-stage artifacts: seed prompts + 10 representative prompt templates (we recommend 1k synthetic prompts covering 90/10 length distribution).
2) Run warm-up job from a single control host (we provide container). Concurrency ramp: 1 -> 10 -> 50 -> target concurrency over 20m total. Keep 30% of requests pinned to the same session ID to exercise KV cache.
3) Monitor 95th percentile latency; stop ramp if p95 > 2x baseline for >5m and reach out to Redwood infra.
4) Final validation: run a 15m soak at expected traffic to confirm stable token/sec and KV hit rates > 60%.

Attachments (stubs):
- autoscale-burst-policy-proposal.pdf
- warmup-runbook.sh (we will share the container + script in the Drive folder)

Next steps:
- Alex / Procurement: confirm the VPC CIDR and sign the SOW addendum once we send it (target Wed Oct 27).
- Olga / Monica: lock the Nov 3-5 window and create the activation ticket.

I'll drop the warmup container and the script into the Drive folder this afternoon.

-Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Onboarding Engineer, Redwood Inference
